newsitem.title: UK: Dixons, Boots shrug off UK market losses.
newsitem.headline: Dixons, Boots shrug off UK market losses.

text.p: Shares in retailers Boots Co Plc and Dixons Group Plc defied the sharp losses elsewhere in the UK equity market on Thursday, bouncing from recent underperformance amid hopes for buoyant Christmas sales, traders said.

Dixons was up 3p at 545-1/2 by 0940 GMT and Boots was up 3p at 605-1/2, even as the FTSE 100 plummeted 39.0 points or 0.95 percent to 4,079.5. However trading volume in both stocks remained relatively thin at 411,206 and 389,340 shares respectively.

"They have underperformed recently and there are some people picking stores to buy for the New Year," said one market-maker. "And the stores have all got trading statements coming out in the next few days."

William Cullum, retail analyst at Paribas Capital Markets, said retail stocks should do well through 1997 though political uncertainties and the threat of higher interest rates were likely to make progress less smooth than in the first part of 1996.

"On the whole the sector is probably a "buy" but it is going to be more volatile than in 1996," Cullum said. "Politics could change things very quickly, but against that there is a reasonably benign outlook on inflation, we have falling unemployment and a buoyant housing market."
Cullum said anecdotal evidence suggested that trading had gone well for the retail sector in the run-up to Christmas and in the recent sales, despite the freezing weather.
"The weather might even have helped clear some of the coats that they didn't shift last year," the Paribas analyst said.
Dixons is due to release its first-half results on January 8. A spokesman for the electrical retailer said the report would include an update on Christmas trading.
At Boots a spokeswoman said the company expected to release Christmas trading information some time in the second week of January.
